what: Comparability caveats by wrapper-type pair, assembled into each cohort's caveat block. Maintained as data (R3): the engine composes prose from these entries, it does not invent them. pricing_class (NAV|MARKET) governs composite refusal; pricing_basis text feeds captions.

interval_23c3.liquidity_law: Rule 23c-3 OBLIGATION (board cannot skip a window)

tender_offer.liquidity_law: board-DISCRETIONARY tender offers (nothing compels the next one)

nontraded_bdc.leverage_regime: BDC 150% asset-coverage regime - materially MORE leverage headroom than 1940-Act funds

nontraded_reit.liquidity_law: share-repurchase plan with monthly/quarterly caps, board may amend or suspend
nontraded_reit.leverage_regime: charter-level borrowing limits; no 1940-Act coverage test

listed_cef.pricing_basis: MARKET PRICE - premium/discount to NAV is the investor's actual basis

listed_bdc.pricing_basis: MARKET PRICE - premium/discount to NAV is the investor's actual basis

pair_caveats.caveat: PRICING-BASIS MIX: some members transact at NAV, others at exchange market price - return comparisons mix appraisal dynamics with premium/discount dynamics; composites across this line are refused, not averaged.
LEVERAGE-REGIME MIX: BDC 150% coverage and non-1940-Act wrappers allow materially more leverage than 1940-Act funds - fee bases and return volatility are not like-for-like.
LIQUIDITY-LAW MIX: Rule 23c-3 obligations, discretionary tenders, and repurchase plans give different worst-case exit rights; cadence numbers alone overstate comparability.
NAV-CADENCE MIX: daily, monthly, and quarterly NAV processes embed different appraisal smoothing; volatility and drawdown comparisons inherit that difference (see de-smoothing lab).
